A '''Cargo Rack''' is an optional internal module that provides cargo capacity, measured in tonnes. Trade, mining, mission-running, and material/commodity-delivery Commanders (including delivering an Engineer's own unlock commodity) all depend on having enough cargo capacity fitted for the job at hand.

== Overview ==

Cargo Racks compete for optional internal slots with every other optional internal module (Shield Generators, Hull Reinforcement Packages, Fuel Scoops, and so on), so a ship's maximum cargo capacity is a build choice rather than a fixed property of the hull.

== Mk II Cargo Racks ==

Update 4.4.2.0 added '''Mk II Cargo Racks''' to the Live game alongside the [[Anaconda Mk II]]. Frontier's October dev log describes the ship's cargo-restricted Size 6 optional compartment as suited to an Optimised Cargo Rack, confirming the Anaconda Mk II's compatibility with the module line.<ref name="anaconda-dev-log">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/elite-dangerous-october-dev-log-2026-law-disorder Elite Dangerous: October Dev Log 2026 — Law & Disorder], Frontier Developments, 14 October 2026.</ref><ref name="anaconda-update">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/updates/4-4-2-0 Elite Dangerous: Anaconda Mk II Update], Frontier Developments, 20 October 2026.</ref>

The same update notes record a fix for a rounding error when engineering Mk II Cargo Racks. This confirms that the modules accept Engineering, although Frontier's public notes do not provide a complete table of compatible classes, capacities, blueprints, or resulting statistics.<ref name="anaconda-update" />

Mk II Cargo Racks are Live-only. Standard Cargo Racks remain available in both Live and Legacy.

== Engineering ==

[[Ram Tah]], based at [[Phoenix Base]] in [[Meene]], is EDFM's currently documented Cargo Rack Engineer. His Cargo Rack blueprint is a Live-only addition that applies only to compatible Merc modules, per the Engineer's own already-sourced article.
